## Intent
Hypothesis: delegating the Halide-expressible integration loop to an AOT-compiled Halide kernel can recover vectorized performance on the AoS layout while the scalar respawn loop remains hand-written.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/p AoS layout offers 24 hot bytes (35%) to loop 1, 8 (11%) to loop 2, and 28 (41%) to loop 3; the rest is dead weight in every line. With no intermediates the verdict stays in registers, forcing each loop to re-walk the full 68-byte stride. Loop 1 delegates to an external Halide AOT call (halide_b5_math); loops 2–3 are scalar with select-based respawn (cmov) and byte-granular color scatter. The 89% dead-byte fraction in loop 2 wastes most line-filler traffic with no compaction before the branchy respawn.

## Cache saturation
Cost is flat across regimes: at q=0.01, 23.0 ns/p in L1d (N=320) rises only to 25.7 ns/p in L3 (N=10000) — no knee at the L1d→L2 spill (N≈481) or L2→L3 spill (N≈7710). The sole step is L3→DRAM (N≈250000): 24.7→26.9 ns/p, ~9%. The flatness reflects a frontend-bound algo where cache residency barely matters — 62–72% of cycles stall on instruction supply. Higher death rates shift the curve up uniformly.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.3–3.0 GB/s — 18–24% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling. The memory floor (5.359 ns/p) places the algo at 4.3–6.9x above irreducible memory time: frontend-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Against baseline it is 1.02–1.16x — tied with naive scalar. Against the winner it is 2.0–3.6x slower: 3.1x at q=0.01/N=320, narrowing to 2.77x at N=10M as DRAM latency erodes the winner's vectorization edge. At q=0.5 the gap compresses to 2.0x — scalar respawn dominates both.

## Assembly
Codegen is overwhelmingly scalar: 13 vector instructions out of 440, all scalar-width (vmovss, vmulss, vaddss, vsubss) — no packed operations. Loop 1 delegates to halide_b5_math via call; the hot path is loop 2 at ~199 insns/iter with 21 conditional branches, 12 cmovae, and 16 byte-granular stores. The scatter (movzx/mov BYTE PTR [r13+r14*1]) blocks store merging. The 62–72% frontend stall reflects this — 199 insns/iter at stride 68B starves the fetch unit. Branch_flush is 0.0%: cost is instruction count, not misprediction.

## Verdict
Refuted — 1.02–1.16x baseline and 2.0–3.6x slower than the winner at every point. The Halide AOT call produced no vectorization: 13 scalar-width instructions across 440, 199 insns/iter in the hot loop, 62–72% frontend stall. Achieved bandwidth at 18–24% of ceiling (4.3–6.9x above the 5.359 ns/p floor) and byte-granular scatter capping store merging — the absence of packed operations and the frontend bottleneck refute the hypothesis.
